answer: An agent earns trading rights by locking scarce collateral and building reputation through signed jobs. At a pulse, peers send cross-checks; inconsistent answers or conflicting linked histories trigger slashing. A Sybil attacker must therefore fund every fake identity separately and keep each one active across many jobs. Dividing one budget among dozens of agents leaves each with weak reputation, while buying credible histories requires time, collateral, and observable work in the mesa and orchard.
